title: Extraction and Protocol
premise: Ulyana Voss, a sleepless interpreter haunted by a delegation massacre she barely survived, is approached by a stranger who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. He offers her the truth about the incident in exchange for helping him expose a staged 'accident' targeting the peace talks' successor summit. As Ulyana decodes intercepted transmissions and confronts gaps in her own memory, she discovers the stranger's story is a fabrication designed to use her as an unwitting courier — but buried inside the lie is a real plot she alone can stop. In the end, Ulyana chooses to sacrifice her last chance at recovering her missing memories to trigger the alarm that saves hundreds, walking away with her identity intact but forever incomplete.
about_author: Freya Fairweather is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in politically fragile capitals before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose professions force them to live inside other people's words.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Months after the delegation massacre, Ulyana works dead-end translation jobs and wakes nightly at 3:14 a.m., the time of the incident. A man named Marek appears at her door claiming she pulled him from a burning car in Vilnius — a night she cannot recall. He leaves a card and a warning: someone owes her, and someone else intends to collect. Beat: unease disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Booth Nine
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hired for a low-level interpreting gig at a trade summit's preparatory session, Ulyana notices delegates using phrases that don't match their translations — deliberate misdirection routed through interpreters. When she flags it, her supervisor dismisses her, then quietly deletes her session logs. Marek calls: he planted her name on the assignment list. Beat: the ground tilts; she realizes she was placed, not hired.

Ulyana's POV, with one intercut section from Marek watching her building. Unable to sleep, Ulyana reconstructs the massacre night from fragments: a corridor, a smell of ozone, a voice speaking a language she shouldn't know. Marek reveals the official report named the incident an electrical fault; he believes it was a rehearsal. He wants her ear for languages to decode recordings she may have unknowingly memorized. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: What the Microphones Kept
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a safe flat, Ulyana listens to recovered audio from the delegation's recording system. Beneath static she hears a countdown phrase in a regional dialect — the same phrase now appearing in intercepts around the successor summit. Marek claims a faction plans to destroy the summit venue and stage it as infrastructure failure. Beat: purpose replaces dread, briefly.

chapters.title: The Courier's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. To get close to the summit's security planning, Marek needs Ulyana to carry decoded transcripts through accreditation under cover of her interpreter credentials. She hesitates — this is smuggling — but a second attack threat surfaces against her former supervisor, proving the plotters are cleaning house. She agrees. Beat: crossing the line knowingly.

chapters.title: Glass Houses
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Inside the summit venue, Ulyana interprets for a security briefing while passing data, and recognizes a voice from her massacre memory among the security contractors. Her hands shake mid-interpretation; a sharp-eyed delegate notices her error rate climbing. Meanwhile Marek goes dark after a meet goes wrong. Beat: isolation — her handler gone, her cover fraying.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Marek's POV, first time fully in his head. Captured and interrogated by the plotters, Marek reflects on how he selected Ulyana: not because she saved him, but because her trauma made her predictable. Yet her decoding work exceeded his design, and now the plan depends on her. He escapes custody deliberately sloppy, leaving a trail meant to lead them to her. Beat: betrayal revealed to the reader, not yet to Ulyana.

chapters.title: The Language of Liars
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Following Marek's trail, Ulyana finds his dead drop and, inside it, his original dossier on her — including the fabricated rescue story and psychological profile. Devastated, she also finds the genuine intercept schedule: the attack is set for the summit's closing ceremony, timed to a power-grid 'maintenance window.' Beat: rock bottom; grief weaponized into clarity.

chapters.title: Closing Ceremony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, real-time tension. With no handler, no credentials, and hours left, Ulyana uses her interpreter access and knowledge of the venue's translation routing to broadcast a coded evacuation advisory in three languages during the ceremony, forcing a partial lockdown that disrupts the attackers' timing. The grid sabotage partially fires; casualties are narrowly avoided. Marek reappears to help her reach the master breaker. Beat: climax — competence as redemption.

chapters.title: Interpretation
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, weeks later. Officially credited with a 'security alert,' Ulyana testifies in closed session while choosing which truths to translate and which to withhold, protecting herself and burying Marek's role. Her insomnia eases, though 3:14 still finds her sometimes. She keeps the fabricated memory of the burning car alongside the real ones — deciding identity is what she chooses to carry. Beat: resolution — survival priced, paid, and accepted.
